solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: It's a bore to smoke

definitions.meaning: something tedious, as in the idiom it's a real nuisance
to draw on a cigarette, take a puff

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a tedious chore is called this in slang, and the same word is the verb for inhaling on a cigarette.

clue.text: See 14
Everyone knows this writer's captivated by awful coterie I won't be part of

indicators.note: held captive inside, so the writer's letters sit within the jumbled group
something awful is a mess, so the remaining letters of coterie are jumbled
the letter I declines to belong, so it is removed from coterie

parts.note: a pen is a writer, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a ghastly clique they refuse to join, and everybody knows it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'won't be part of' removes the I from the clique; 'awful' rearranges the remaining six letters into O and ECRET, and 'captivated by' puts the writer's letters between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A fact that is supposedly confidential but in practice is common knowledge.

clue.text: Service provided for big rock group?

parts.note: Mass is a church service
provided means if, as in provided that

explanation.surface: A church service laid on for a famous rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big rock group' suggests a band; it is a group of mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Geological term for a compact cluster of mountains, a large group of rocky peaks.

clue.text: Navy vessels almost all kept in readiness, not like the fastest jets

parts.note: subs are submarines

indicators.note: nearly the whole phrase, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: on ice means held in reserve, kept ready

explanation.surface: The navy holds most of its craft on standby, unlike the speediest aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost all' removes the final E of ON ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Slower than sound, whereas the quickest jets are supersonic.

clue.text: Something troubling your eye, primarily

indicators.note: in the first place, so the opening letter of each of the four words is taken

explanation.surface: Mainly, it is something bothering your eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both defines and, via 'primarily', supplies the initials of its first four words.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflamed swelling on the eyelid, which is an irritation to the eye.

clue.text: Give up repeated attempt to get ball airborne

parts.note: drop means abandon or give up
say give up again with a second word: kick, as in quitting a habit

explanation.surface: Abandoning a second effort to get a ball into the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeated' asks for give up a second time, by another synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby, a kick made as the dropped ball bounces, used to send it up toward goal.

clue.text: Druid-supporting poster put up in effort to influence public opinion

parts.note: pro means in favour of, and a Druid is a pagan

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A placard backing the Druids is hung up as part of a campaign for hearts and minds.
explanation.definitionFit: Information, often biased, spread to sway how people think.

clue.text: Go over summit after moment of hesitation's rejected

indicators.note: the summit comes behind the turned hesitation
sent back, so the hesitation reads backwards

parts.note: er is the sound of a pause in speech
a cap is a top

explanation.surface: Someone revisits a summit after their wavering is overruled.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for recapitulate: to run through the main points again.

clue.text: Dater involved with breaking rule?

indicators.note: both words are mixed up: involved and breaking are each signals of rearrangement

explanation.surface: Is someone who dates while breaking the rules a cheat?
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of DATER and RULE are mixed together, and the whole clue describes the cheating spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A married person who takes up with someone else, breaking the marital rule of fidelity.

clue.text: Sediment surrounding garden

definitions.meaning: dregs settling at the bottom, as of coffee
the land and gardens around a building

explanation.definitionFit: Coffee dregs are one sense; the estate around a house is the other.

clue.text: Clean little dog after end of Crufts

indicators.note: the small dog follows the final letter
the final letter of the dog show's name

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: A small dog is washed once the dog show is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Crufts is Britain's best-known dog show.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb for tidying up by brushing debris together.

clue.text: Own about a pound then make 50p?

indicators.note: around, so possess wraps the pound

parts.note: to have is to possess
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone holds a pound and then turns it into fifty pence.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut into two equal parts, as fifty pence is half a pound.

clue.text: What riders require, and publicans are required to do

definitions.meaning: the steering grips of a bicycle
pub landlords have to manage, run their bars

explanation.definitionFit: Cyclists grip the steering bar; read as two words it says publicans must manage the bars.

clue.text: Polish girls here maybe foolishly choosing to be detained by heartless Nordic lecturer

indicators.note: held inside, so the jumble sits within the other letters
losing its heart, the middle letter, so one N goes

parts.note: Finnish describes Finland, a Nordic land

indicators.note: done in a foolish, muddled way, so the letters of choosing are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some silly girls choose to be held back by a Scandinavian teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality; it is the verb, refine. The jumbled letters of 'choosing' go just before the lecturer's L.
explanation.definitionFit: A private college where young women were taught social graces, a place to refine girls.

clue.text: Male wearing item of clothing mostly seen on female causes scuffles

indicators.note: in a down clue, sitting on top means coming first
most of the garment, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a skirt is a garment

indicators.note: having on, so the clothing and title surround the male

parts.note: Miss is a title for a woman
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man in a woman's garment provokes some fights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' reads as dressed in, but here the male pronoun sits inside the female title, after the shortened garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief fights or minor clashes, synonyms for small scraps.

clue.text: Old bird out of bounds?

definitions.meaning: a fowl that has lost its bounce, unable to leap

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means past one's youth; read literally it is a hen without bounce.

clue.text: Wisdom of Storyville?

parts.note: split the answer in two: a saga is a story and a city is a ville, a town

explanation.definitionFit: Sound judgement or shrewdness, a synonym for wisdom.

clue.text: Stops working, coming into category of those with no job or training, extremely deserving

indicators.note: entering, so the breakdown sits inside the category

parts.words: category of those with no job or training
parts.note: NEET stands for not in education, employment or training
a machine dies when it breaks down

explanation.surface: Breakdown hits the unemployed group, making them the most deserving.
explanation.walkthrough: NEET is a UK label for a young person not in education, employment or training.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of needy: the most in want, the most deserving of help.

clue.text: A long way from home for soldiers, heading off to eastern Arabia

indicators.note: the first letter is removed

parts.note: Blighty is soldiers' slang for Britain, home

explanation.surface: Soldiers far from home head off to the Arabian east.
explanation.walkthrough: BLIGHTY, troops' slang for Britain, loses its B.
explanation.definitionFit: The distance light travels in twelve months, an enormous span.

clue.text: Animal home amid rubbish

indicators.note: in the middle of, so the lair sits inside the nonsense

parts.note: rot means nonsense
a den is an animal's lair

explanation.surface: A creature makes its lair among the litter.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnawing mammal such as a rat or mouse.

clue.text: Mother packs key for Mediterranean island

indicators.note: holds within, so mother encloses the key

parts.note: ma is mum
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: Mum puts a key in her luggage before going to the Med.
explanation.definitionFit: An island nation lying south of Sicily.

clue.text: Fire head of accounts just after start of meal

indicators.note: placed directly behind the first letter, so it goes inside next to the opening

parts.note: lunch is a midday meal

indicators.note: the first letter of accounts

explanation.surface: A boss sacks the head of accounts right after the meal begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' suggests sacking; it is shooting off a rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: To send off a missile or rocket, synonyms for discharge.

clue.text: Germs in second-rate air-conditioning bringing misfortune to island

parts.note: B is second class
ill means trouble, harm

explanation.surface: Poor air-conditioning spreads germs that bring trouble to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Rod-shaped bacteria, some of which cause disease.

clue.text: Laugh out loud with a senorita?

parts.note: LOL is texting shorthand for laugh out loud

explanation.surface: Laughing heartily with a young Spanish woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish girl's name, so an example of a senorita.

clue.text: Treat disrespectfully and swear in debate

parts.note: dis is slang for insult
cuss means curse

explanation.surface: Insulting and cursing during an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk over or argue about a matter, a synonym for debate.

clue.text: Drop agreement made verbally

indicators.note: spoken, so the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: in sync means in agreement, in step

explanation.surface: Withdrawing a deal that was only spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop' suggests abandoning the deal; it means fall downward.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall or go down, as a stone does in water.

clue.text: Toy for baby — boy won't stop chattering

parts.note: a rattle is an infant's toy
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A baby's toy for a lad who talks nonstop.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb meaning talks at length without pause.

clue.text: Old time-server is political turncoat perhaps

definitions.meaning: a former prisoner who did time
a former Conservative who switched party

explanation.definitionFit: A released prisoner, or read differently someone who left the Tories.
